arxiv-1912-11692.title: Thermostatic control for demand response using distributed averaging and deep neural networks
arxiv-1912-11692.creator: Kshitij Singh, Pratik Bajaria
arxiv-1912-11692.description: Abstract Smart buildings are the need of the day with increasing demand-supply ratios and deficiency to generate considerably. In any modern non-industrial infrastructure, these demands mainly comprise of thermostatically controlled loads (TCLs), which can be manoeuvred. TCL loads like air-conditioner, heater, refrigerator, are ubiquitous, and their operating times can be controlled to achieve desired aggregate power.

arxiv-2007-12282.title: On Positivity and Minimality for Second-Order Holonomic Sequences
arxiv-2007-12282.creator: George Kenison, Oleksiy Klurman, Engel Lefaucheux, Florian Luca, Pieter Moree, Joël Ouaknine, Markus A. Whiteland, James Worrell
arxiv-2007-12282.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by George Kenison, Oleksiy Klurman, Engel Lefaucheux, Florian Luca, Pieter Moree, Joël Ouaknine, Markus A. Whiteland, James Worrell. An infinite sequence ⟨ u n ⟩ n ∈ ℕ \langle u_{n}\rangle_{n\in\mathbb{N}} of real numbers is holonomic (also known as P P -recursive or P P -finite ) if it satisfies a linear recurrence relation with polynomial coefficients.

Proceedings of the 27th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery
arxiv-2106-01682.creator: Olivier Sprangers, Sebastian Schelter, Maarten de Rijke
arxiv-2106-01682.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Olivier Sprangers, Sebastian Schelter, Maarten de Rijke. GBM are hugely popular for solving tabular data problems. However, practitioners are not only interested in point predictions, but also in probabilistic predictions in order to quantify the uncertainty of the predictions. Creating such probabilistic predictions is difficult with existing GBM -based solutions: they either require training multiple models or they become too computationally expensive to be useful for large-scale settings.

arxiv-2203-07260.title: SimHawNet : A Modified Hawkes Process for Temporal Network Simulation
arxiv-2203-07260.creator: Mathilde Perez, Raphaël Romero, Bo Kang, Tijl De Bie, Jefrey Lijffijt, Charlotte Laclau
arxiv-2203-07260.description: Abstract Temporal networks allow representing connections between objects while incorporating the temporal dimension. While static network models can capture unchanging topological regularities, they often fail to model the effects associated with the causal generative process of the network that occurs in time. Hence, exploiting the temporal aspect of networks has been the focus of many recent studies.

arxiv-2302-09114.title: Smoothly Giving up: Robustness for Simple Models
arxiv-2302-09114.creator: Tyler Sypherd, Nathan Stromberg, Richard Nock, Visar Berisha, Lalitha Sankar
arxiv-2302-09114.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tyler Sypherd, Nathan Stromberg, Richard Nock, Visar Berisha, Lalitha Sankar. There is a growing need for models that are interpretable and have reduced energy and computational cost (e.g., in health care analytics and federated learning). Examples of algorithms to train such models include logistic regression and boosting.

arxiv-2306-03592.title: A sketch-and-select Arnoldi process
arxiv-2306-03592.creator: Stefan Güttel, Igor Simunec
arxiv-2306-03592.description: Abstract A sketch-and-select Arnoldi process to generate a well-conditioned basis of a Krylov space at low cost is proposed. At each iteration the procedure utilizes randomized sketching to select a limited number of previously computed basis vectors to project out of the current basis vector. The computational cost grows linearly with the dimension of the Krylov space.

arxiv-2405-13452.title: Search for single vector-like B B quark production in hadronic final states at the LHC
arxiv-2405-13452.creator: Bingfang Yang 1 , Zejun Li 1 , Xinglong Jia 1 , Stefano Moretti 2,3 , and Liangliang Shang 1,2
arxiv-2405-13452.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the discovery potential of a Vector-Like B B quark (VLB) via the process p p → B ( → b Z ) j → b ( Z → ν l ν l ¯ ) j pp\to B(\to bZ)j\to b(Z\to\nu_{l}\bar{\nu_{l}})j at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) with s = 14 \sqrt{s}=14 TeV.

arxiv-2501-11914.title: LuxVeri at GenAI Detection Task 1: Inverse Perplexity Weighted Ensemble for Robust Detection of AI-Generated Text across English and Multilingual Contexts
arxiv-2501-11914.creator: Md Kamrujjaman Mobin, Md Saiful Islam
arxiv-2501-11914.description: Abstract This paper presents a system developed for Task 1 of the COLING 2025 Workshop on Detecting AI-Generated Content, focusing on the binary classification of machine-generated versus human-written text. Our approach utilizes an ensemble of models, with weights assigned according to each model’s inverse perplexity, to enhance classification accuracy.

arxiv-2501-16559.title: LoRA-X: Bridging Foundation Models with Training-Free Cross-Model Adaptation
arxiv-2501-16559.creator: Farzad Farhadzadeh, Debasmit Das, Shubhankar Borse, Fatih Porikli, Qualcomm AI Research, San Diego, CA 92121, USA {ffarhadz, debadas, sborse, fporikli}@qti.qualcomm.com
arxiv-2501-16559.description: Abstract The rising popularity of large foundation models has led to a heightened demand for parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods, such as Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), which offer performance comparable to full model fine-tuning while requiring only a few additional parameters tailored to the specific base model.

arxiv-2505-00703.title: T2I-R1: Reinforcing Image Generation with Collaborative Semantic-level and Token-level CoT
arxiv-2505-00703.creator: Dongzhi Jiang, Ziyu Guo, Renrui Zhang, Zhuofan Zong, Hao Li, Le Zhuo, Shilin Yan, Pheng-Ann Heng, Hongsheng Li
arxiv-2505-00703.description: Abstract Recent advancements in large language models have demonstrated how chain-of-thought (CoT) and reinforcement learning (RL) can improve performance. However, applying such reasoning strategies to the visual generation domain remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we present T2I-R1 , a novel reasoning-enhanced text-to-image generation model, powered by RL with a bi-level CoT reasoning process.

arxiv-2506-21110.title: Orthogonality conditions for convex regression E-mail addresses: sheng.dai@zuel.edu.cn (S. Dai) , timo.kuosmanen@utu.fi (T. Kuosmanen) , x.zhou@surrey.ac.uk (X. Zhou) .
arxiv-2506-21110.creator: Sheng Dai, Timo Kuosmanen, Xun Zhou
arxiv-2506-21110.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sheng Dai, Timo Kuosmanen, Xun Zhou. Econometric identification generally relies on orthogonality conditions, which usually state that the random error term is uncorrelated with the explanatory variables. In convex regression, the orthogonality conditions for identification are unknown. Applying Lagrangian duality theory, we establish the sample orthogonality conditions for convex regression, including additive and multiplicative formulations of the regression model, with and without monotonicity and homogeneity constraints.

arxiv-2507-01751.title: Black hole optical analogue: photon sphere microlasers
arxiv-2507-01751.creator: Chenni Xu 1§, Aswathy Sundaresan 1§, Nazire-Begüm Kazkal 2, Clement Lafargue 3, Lior Zarfaty 1, Li-Gang Wang 4, Ofek Birnholtz 1, Dominique Decanini 2, Melanie Lebental 2, Patrick Sebbah 1
arxiv-2507-01751.description: Abstract The bell-like ringdown of the gravitational field in the last stage of the merging of massive black holes is now routinely detected on earth by the last generation of gravitational wave detectors. Its spectrum is interpreted as a sum of damped sinusoidal vibrations of the spacetime in the vicinity of the black hole.

pmc-10762588.title: Parathyroid adenoma apoplexy mimicking a thyroid bleeding cyst: a seemingly innocent condition that can be life-threatening
pmc-10762588.creator: Jasmine Van de Kerkhof, Jacqueline Bijnens, Frank De Geeter, Catherine Dick, Pascale De Paepe, Annick Van den Bruel
pmc-10762588.description: SummaryPrimary hyperparathyroidism most commonly presents with hypercalcaemia. Rarely, parathyroid apoplexy or haemorrhage mimicking a thyroid bleeding cyst is the first presentation of a parathyroid adenoma. A woman presented with a sudden-onset painful ‘goitre’. Ultrasound showed a cystic nodule located posterior to rather than in the right thyroid lobe, suggesting parathyroid adenoma bleeding. Biochemistry showed mild primary hyperparathyroidism.

pmc-11710401.title: Neuroprotective potential of quetiapine against streptozotocin‐induced sporadic Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11710401.creator: Shilpa Kumari, Paras Attri, Rahul Renukadas Deshmukh
pmc-11710401.description: BackgroundIn previous studies, we found that quetiapine activates the AKT signaling which further inhibits the action of GSK3β. Quetiapine has been reported to possess neuroprotective potential in schizophrenia and other neurodegenerative models.MethodOn day 1st and 3rd, rats received bilateral intracerebroventricular (i.c.v.) administration of STZ (3 mg/kg).

pmc-12549947.title: Evolution of prediabetes in an urban cohort of adults living in a Mediterranean area
pmc-12549947.creator: Carola Buscemi, Cristiana Randazzo, Anna Maria Barile, Rosalia Caldarella, Alexis Elias Malavazos, Roberta Caruso, Piero Colombrita, Martina Lombardo, Silvio Buscemi
pmc-12549947.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPrediabetes (PD) precedes type 2 diabetes (T2D), it can be easily recognized by fasting plasma glucose concentrations (FPG) or HbA1c or 2 h post glucose load glycemia, thereby enabling prevention strategies. We investigated the progression of PD to T2D in the ABCD study (Alimentazione, Benessere Cardiovascolare e Diabete -ISRCTN15840340) that included a representative cohort of adult people living in the Mediterranean area of Palermo (Italy).Materials and methodsThe ABCD cohort was enrolled in 2011 and re-evaluated in 2015.

pmc-12583862.description: Multiple myeloma (MM) and stem cell transplantation (SCT) significantly impact patients’ quality of life. pmc-13035083.description: BackgroundMedication adherence among patients with cancer is generally low. Mobile health (mHealth) has gradually been applied to improve this situation, but systematic evidence of its effectiveness remains lacking.ObjectiveWe aimed to evaluate the effect of mHealth on improving medication adherence among patients with cancer.

pmc-13146240.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A789 PREVALENCE AND CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS OF STROKE MIMICS AMONG PATIENTS WITH SUSPECTED ACUTE STROKE IN THE EMERGENCY

pmc-13146240.description: Background and aimsObjective: Stroke mimics present a diagnostic challenge in the emergency department (ED). We aimed to determine the prevalence, aetiologies, and clinical predictors of stroke mimics in patients presenting with suspected acute stroke within 9 hours of symptom onset.

pmc-13280034.title: Specific Markers of Knee Morphology are Associated with Osteochondritis Dissecans of the Medial Femoral Condyle in Pediatric and Adolescent Patients: A Matched Case-Control Study

pmc-13412251.title: Beyond the Neutrophil Count: Functional Profiling and Targeted Modulation of Neutrophils in Paediatric Care
pmc-13412251.creator: James Trayer, Lynne A. Kelly, Eoghan Dunlea, Dearbhla Byrne, Nicoleta Barbu, Eleanor J. Molloy
pmc-13412251.description: BackgroundNeutrophils are the most abundant leukocytes in childhood and form a critical component of innate immunity, particularly in early life when adaptive responses are still maturing. In paediatrics, both quantitative and qualitative disturbances in neutrophil number or function shape susceptibility to infection and inflammatory tissue injury.

pmc-13463202.title: Harmonizing biomarker testing in NSCLC: The critical role of cytopathology in delivering comprehensive biomarker testing for patients with NSCLC
pmc-13463202.creator: Sinchita Roy‐Chowdhuri, Haresh Mani
pmc-13463202.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 1 Therapeutic decisions increasingly depend on comprehensive molecular profiling and biomarker assessment based on the testing recommendations from clinical practice guidelines. 2 In a recent article in Cancer, 3 Patel and colleagues present a timely analysis of biomarker testing recommendations across major professional society guidelines and highlight an often‐overlooked challenge in clinical decision‐making: variability in guideline interpretation and implementation despite broad agreement on fundamental principles.

pmc-13561052.title: Evaluation of the impact of donor site size on treatment outcomes in experimental deep second-degree burns treated with non-cultured autologous cell spray
pmc-13561052.creator: Sermet Terzi, Ömer Cennet, Busenur Kırımtay, Kemal Kösemehmetoğlu, Ali Konan
pmc-13561052.description: BACKGROUNDDeep second-degree burn treatment is often time-consuming and expensive, with split-thickness autografts being the current standard of care. Recently, noncultured autologous cell sprays have shown comparable efficacy. This study utilized an experimental animal model to determine the optimal donor-to-burn area ratio for this method.

pmc-13583092.title: Early Clinical and Cerebrospinal Fluid Predictors of 1‐Year Recurrence in Autoimmune GFAP Astrocytopathy
pmc-13583092.creator: Qingting Hong, Yuping Xiao, Yuhan Wu, Ziyuan Huang, Weishan Liang, Li Xiao, Yaqing Shu, Tingting Lu, Yanyu Chang, Wei Qiu, Yuge Wang
pmc-13583092.description: ObjectiveAutoimmune glial fibrillary acidic protein astrocytopathy (GFAP‐A) is an inflammatory central nervous system disorder with variable outcomes. Relapse occurs in a subset of patients, but early predictors remain unclear. We aimed to identify admission‐available features associated with 1‐year recurrence and develop an interpretable risk stratification model.MethodsWe retrospectively included 156 patients with CSF GFAP‐IgG‐positive GFAP‐A between January 2021 and February 2025.
